# `list identities` is the full identity record per row — the view `list roles`
# (name+roles only) and `ps` (identities paired with locks) each show part of.
# This covers the rendering end-to-end against a real daemon, including the two
# things that are invisible in a single run: sort order and the mess-target column.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

# Registered deliberately out of alphabetical order, so insertion order and sorted
# order differ. Before Identities() sorted, this table came back in a different
# order on every call — nothing errored, it just rendered differently each time.
exec breeze register identity zeta
exec breeze register identity alpha
cp stdout alpha.token
exec breeze register identity mid --mess-agent other-agent

exec breeze list identities
stdout 'IDENTITY[\s\S]*ROLES[\s\S]*TOKEN[\s\S]*MESS TARGET[\s\S]*REGISTERED'
# Sorted by name: alpha, then mid, then zeta — NOT the order they registered in.
stdout 'alpha[\s\S]*mid[\s\S]*zeta'

# An identity with no explicit --mess-agent notifies under its own name; one with
# a mapping shows the agent it actually resolves to. The row worth spotting is the
# one that DIFFERS, so the default is rendered "= name" rather than repeated.
stdout 'alpha[\s\S]*= name'
stdout 'mid[\s\S]*other-agent'

# Every identity here was minted with a token, so none should read "none".
! stdout 'alpha\s+\S*\s+none'

# Same data, machine-readable — the flag every other list command takes.
exec breeze list identities --json
stdout '"name":\s*"alpha"'
stdout '"messAgent":\s*"other-agent"'

# The singular noun routes to the same place (see route.go's nouns list).
exec breeze list identity
stdout 'IDENTITY'

exec breeze stop
